title: Fixed-synapse spiking threshold task views
amendment: 02: amendment 01 completed calculations but stopped while printing a JSON summary due to a misplaced flush argument; its output is retained separately and excluded
scope: Mechanism-only synthetic threshold bank; not an STL-SNN reproduction or neuromorphic energy claim.
hypothesis: An affine task coordinate (base plus task-index times step) can replace a bank of independent per-task firing thresholds with lower serialized bytes while retaining each threshold classifier; an irregular threshold bank will expose the private-residual boundary.
physical_object: One shared scalar synapse and one deterministic leaky integrate-and-fire neuron, evaluated for each task threshold.
mirror_coordinate: Task index m selects theta_m = base + step*m; optional fitted private residuals are charged in full.
logical_multiplicity: Sixteen task-specific one-dimensional decision boundaries. This is a synthetic threshold family, not sixteen independent neural classifiers.

training.threshold_source: predefined synthetic teacher thresholds; no learned parameters

success_gate: On every fresh world, affine coordinate accuracy is at least 99% of FP32 threshold accuracy and full serialized payload is at least 20% smaller; report spike counts and compare direct 4-bit quantization.
failure_gate: Any quality/byte gate miss or direct quantization matches the Mirror coordinate at equal/fewer bytes.
boundaries: The code is compared to native scalar threshold parameterizations and direct quantization.
Exact arithmetic progression is not Mirror-specific if ordinary parameter coding matches.
No learned SNN, natural event data, energy joules, or hardware efficiency claim.
implementation_history: Amendment 01 wrote metrics but exited on a summary-printing TypeError before run completion; preserved as source/amendment01_unmatched.* and excluded from reported result.
Amendment 02 fixes summary printing and uses three new seeds fixed before rerun.
